newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares recover after fall below 1,600pts.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares recover after fall below 1,600pts.

text.p: The French election outcome was cited by brokers as the prime reason for an extension of the losing streak at the Athens bourse, sparked off in the previous week in reaction to rising interbank rates and a softer drachma.
Brokers said the market was affected by the French elections outcome due to increased concern from foreign investors, while domestic investors remained resilient.

"The French election election outcome has influenced sentiment but this is more evident on the part of the bourse's foreign component," a floor trader said. "There is particular pressure in typical foreign portfolio holdings such as Alpha Credit and ErgoBank."
At current price levels there is fresh buying interst surfacing, the trader added.
Other market watchers said the reasons for last week's drop had been removed.
"The turbulance in the forex market which forced a blip in interest rates has withered away," said Maria Lentziou, an analyst at Olympic Securities.
The part-flotation and rights issue of state telecoms OTE in the coming months was not seen draining liquidity from the broader market.

"The interest of people who are not familiar with equities in OTE's new issue indicates that there should be no concern of a liquidity drain on other stocks," said Lentziou. The government's moves in the field of interest rates and its ability to harness inflation would be the focus in the coming months.
"The fall in nominal interest rates has narrowed real interest rate differentials, requiring increased caution on the drachma as the experience of the previous week showed," Lentziou said.
Technical analysts suggested that prices would remain rangebound in the near-term.

"There is a strong support level at 1,600 points and the index is expected to oscillate between 1,600 and 1,695 in the near-term. Short-term indicators, including the RSI, have corrected considerably and the medium-term price oscillator has not given an exit signal," said Omega Securities.
Wide price fluctuations and nervousness are part of the adjustment process to price levels unseen for several years, it added.
Construction analysts said they expected construction stocks to be overshadowed by developments in other sectors in the near-term.
"Other sectors such as banks, industrials and telecoms will remain in the limelight for the coming few months," said a construction analyst.
Despite an acceleration in awards of public works, there is no market-moving news for the sector before a decision for the 2004 Olympic Games in September is announced, he added.
Along with Rome, the city of Athens is considered a prime candidate for staging the 2004 games which will necessitate widespread heavy construction works.

The Athens general index was off 0.78 percent or 11.39 points to 1,622.56 from Friday's 1,635.31 close after 40 minutes of trading, recovering from a low of 1,596.02 touched some 15 minutes after the open.
Banks and industrials led the market with a 1.41 percent fall.
Turnover was heavy at 10.1 billion on volume of 1.3 million shares.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 1,114-1,144. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were up 150 drachmas at 6,950 drachmas.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 648.57-689.96. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $81.69-$83.39. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,749-3,975 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $17.18-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 261-293 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
--Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
